justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I assessed as the prevailing price level at the time of the forecast, which appeared to be in the low-to-mid 580s range. For the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the recent price with minimal drift, since short-term mean reversion and momentum tend to dominate over very brief windows. For the one-week estimate, I nudged the target slightly higher to around 587, reflecting a mild continuation of any prevailing trend without assuming a strong directional catalyst. The one-month estimate of 595 extends that gentle upward bias further, consistent with the long-run tendency of broad equity indices to drift higher over multi-week periods in the absence of severe macro disruption. None of these point estimates assume a dramatic breakout or breakdown; they are essentially trend extrapolations with a slight positive bias.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect how uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, realized volatility for an instrument like SPY or a major index tends to run in the range of 0.5–1.5% on an average session, which translates to a fairly tight band. Over one week, daily fluctuations accumulate, and any single day with elevated volatility — a surprise economic print, a Fed speaker, geopolitical news — can shift the weekly range meaningfully. By one month, the cone widens considerably because there are roughly twenty trading sessions in which any number of macro or earnings-related surprises can compound. The 90% confidence interval at one month spanning roughly 120 points reflects that a one-standard-deviation monthly move in major indices often falls in the 4–7% range.

Several risks could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, an unexpected credit event, a sharp deterioration in economic data suggesting recession, or an abrupt Federal Reserve policy shift could send prices well below the lower bound of the one-month interval. A resurgence of geopolitical conflict affecting energy prices or global supply chains could also produce a rapid repricing. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected earnings season, a surprise dovish pivot from central banks, or a resolution of trade tensions could drive prices meaningfully above 655 within a month. Liquidity conditions and options market dynamics, such as a gamma squeeze or forced dealer hedging, represent additional tail risks that are difficult to model with standard distributional assumptions and could accelerate moves in either direction beyond what my intervals capture.
